macwhisper:speakerkit.when: Diarization support: pyannote (segmenter/embedder v3, clusterer v4), 32 MB. Must be local for --speakers to survive an eject.

macwhisper:speakerkit-pro.when: Diarization support: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 (sortformer), up to 8 speakers, 74 MB. Must be local for --speakers to survive an eject.

ollama:gemma4:26b-nvfp4.when: Fast-context chat model (MLX works for gemma). Use when you want to paste big text and get quick answers. NOT a coding-agent replacement.
ollama:gemma4:26b-nvfp4.speed: ~314 tok/s prompt-eval, ~27 tok/s decode (measured 2026-07-24, 35K-tok file, COLD, num_ctx unrecorded) (value lost to a CLI truncation bug; model max context is 262144 per ollama show, 2026-09-30)
ollama:gemma4:26b-nvfp4.tested: 2026-07-24: best local big-file summarizer — fastest prefill of installed models + 262K ctx. ~2min cold for 35K tokens. Tight, accurate. | 2026-09-25: best of 4 for short structured dashboard summaries (claude-sessions-board, ~500-tok prompt, TITLE line + 2 sentences): TITLE format held every run, specific titles; still opened 2 of 5 live summaries with a banned "The session" (all 4 models slip on that rule). 12s cold load from AI-LAB, ~0.6s warm; ~3.4s avg over 15 live board summaries. First pick when docked.

ollama:gemma4:e4b.when: Lean local summarizer for small files (llmsummarize auto routes <~8K tokens here). NOTE: default runtime ctx self-caps at 16384 — raise num_ctx or it silently truncates big files.
ollama:gemma4:e4b.speed: ~269 tok/s prompt-eval, ~33 tok/s decode (measured 2026-07-24, 35K-tok file, COLD, num_ctx unrecorded) (value lost to a CLI truncation bug; model max context is 131072 per ollama show, 2026-09-30)
ollama:gemma4:e4b.tested: 2026-07-24: good plain-prose summaries, fastest decode of the 4 general models. Silently truncated 34K-tok input to 16K until num_ctx raised. | 2026-09-25: weak on short structured summaries (claude-sessions-board): dropped the required TITLE: label once, broke a 'no "The session"' rule. Use gemma4:26b-nvfp4 instead when docked.

ollama:llama3.1:8b.when: General chat fallback when you want a non-MLX / non-Gemma flavor. 14 months old; keep only if you have prompts tuned to llama3.
ollama:llama3.1:8b.speed: ~142 tok/s prompt-eval, ~16 tok/s decode (measured 2026-07-24, 33K-tok file, COLD) — slowest prefill+decode of installed general models
ollama:llama3.1:8b.tested: 2026-07-24: worst prefill (~4min for 33K tokens). Summary accurate but no reason to pick over gemma for summarization.

ollama:muse-glimmer:30b-mlx.when: UNTESTED MLX variant, kept alongside :latest. Bench later with clean/available memory (close cmux; a num_ctx limit was noted here but lost to a CLI truncation bug; model max context is 131072 per ollama show, 2026-09-30)
ollama:muse-glimmer:30b-mlx.speed: UNTESTED on M2 Max. nvfp4/MLX prefill is a coin-flip here (gemma nvfp4 ~314 tok/s vs qwen3.5 nvfp4 collapsed to 3 tok/s) — MUST measure, do not assume.
ollama:muse-glimmer:30b-mlx.tested: 2026-08-13: NOT yet cleanly benched. An earlier load was noted, but its num_ctx value was lost to a CLI truncation bug (model max context is 131072 per ollama show, 2026-09-30).

ollama:muse-glimmer:latest.when: Primary local vision model — the ONLY installed model with image input (CLIP 1.9B projector). Same build Slava runs (M1 Max/64GB). ~18GB, fits normal headroom. Use for multimodal/vision + agentic tasks.
ollama:muse-glimmer:latest.speed: Untested here; GGUF Q4_K_M so expect the known-safe prefill path (qwen3-coder GGUF ~110 tok/s analog), NOT the MLX coin-flip. Bench when convenient.
ollama:muse-glimmer:latest.tested: 2026-08-13: 27.9B Q4_K_M GGUF, vision+tools+thinking, 131072 ctx, temp default 1 (override to 0 for bench). Not yet benched on this Mac.

ollama:nimble:9b-q4_K_M.when: Jev-style System One decision model (/v1/systemone). Best local pick for score/rubric primitives; too slow and low-confidence for interactive use. Prompt hard-capped (8,192 tok per JT's earlier run).
ollama:nimble:9b-q4_K_M.speed: ~3.3s mean on 1-3 question cases, ~12-15s on 15-question score cases (M2 Max, warm, 2026-10-06)
ollama:nimble:9b-q4_K_M.tested: 2026-10-06 jev:compare, 17 fixtures vs human labels: 74% overall (score 63%, choice 73%, noul 90%); beats qwen3.5:9b on score (63 vs 23%), loses on choice (73 vs 80%); confidence poorly calibrated (79% acc at conf>=0.66, n=57). Apache 2.0. Re-pulled for this bench; AI-LAB only. | 2026-10-06 cold start (spotlight-0, all models unloaded first, Ollama 0.40): first request 6.2s / 4.6s, warm ~0.14s, so load ~4.4-6.0s.

ollama:qwen2.5-coder:1.5b.when: Cron: rename-claude-sessions title generator. Tiny, 152 tok/s.

ollama:qwen2.5-coder:7b.when: Fast coder fallback when qwen3-coder feels heavy.
ollama:qwen2.5-coder:7b.tested: 2026-09-25: bad for instruction-following summaries (claude-sessions-board): copied the input's title verbatim 3/3 runs, broke a phrasing rule. Code model; don't use for prose.

ollama:qwen3-coder:latest.when: Primary coding agent (aider/pi). Tool-calling strong; decode fast.

ollama:qwen3.5:9b.when: General, thinking-capable summarizer (GGUF Q4). Mid-pack prefill. think:false REQUIRED for plain tasks (else ~80s internal monologue). Also the local Jev / TypeSafe System One stand-in for typed decisions (classify, route, yes/no, triage) with confidence: chat + think:false + temperature 0 + one-word labels with distinct first tokens, read top_logprobs. Tied the dedicated Jev-style decision model nimble:9b (removed), faster.
ollama:qwen3.5:9b.speed: ~225 tok/s prompt-eval, ~21 tok/s decode (measured 2026-07-24, 34K-tok file, COLD, think:false)
ollama:qwen3.5:9b.tested: 2026-07-24: most-detailed/accurate summary of the 4, but ~1.4x slower prefill than gemma4:26b. Not 'catastrophic' — that graveyard note was the nvfp4 variant, not this GGUF. | 2026-09-25: runner-up for short structured dashboard summaries (claude-sessions-board, think:false): format OK, titles sometimes vague, once broke a 'no "The session"' rule. 29s cold, 0.7s warm. On both stores, so the undocked fallback. | 2026-09-30: session-state classifier (done/waiting/working, last agent message, think:false, chat logprobs for confidence): 92% holdout (35/38), 87% dev; 1.2-1.5s. p(done)>=0.85 wrongly flagged 4/91, found 61/68 done. Tied with nimble:9b decision model, which was removed. Labels must start with distinct single-token words for logprobs. Bench: private/decision-model-bench/ | 2026-10-05: PR review judgments (bench private/decision-model-bench/pr-threads/). Thread state: content-only addressed/declined/open + code-derived waiting = 98% holdout (43/44), OPEN->ADDRESSED 0/14; asking it for waiting directly = 73%. Feedback actionable/question/fyi 78-94% holdout depending on prompt; errors sit at conf<0.66 (stale-nudge comments flip to question at ~0.5). 3.4s warm per thread, 1.4-2s per comment, 6-13s cold. | 2026-10-06 cold start via chat logprobs (Jev stand-in, spotlight-0, local store): first request 9.5s / 7.5s, warm 0.12-0.14s. WARNING: Ollama 0.40.0 cannot load it from the AI-LAB store ('manifest symlink target ... is not a sha256 blob'); only works against the local store (~/.ollama-local-models). | 2026-10-06: AI-LAB load fixed — aimodels reconcile now copies manifests instead of symlinking them; verified ollama show/run on the AI-LAB store, Ollama 0.40.0.

ollama:tev1:0.8b.when: Smallest System One decision model (0.8B, 811 MB). Fastest local Jev stand-in (~0.26s/case); same 2,050-token prompt cap as tev1:4b. Fine for low-stakes yes/no and short routing, with worse calibration.
ollama:tev1:0.8b.tested: 2026-10-06 jev:compare vs human labels, 28 accepted questions: 89% (choice 88%, noul 90%) but Brier 0.25 vs 0.11 for tev1:4b; errors at conf 0.48-0.57 plus one confident miss (spotlight-5 said 'none'). Skipped same 3 cases as 4b. AI-LAB only. | 2026-10-06 cold start (spotlight-0): first request 1.6s / 1.1s, warm ~0.05s. Cheapest cold start.

ollama:tev1:4b.when: Together AI tev1 System One decision model, 4B. Credible fast Jev stand-in for choice and yes/no primitives in short prompts; cannot take a prompt over 2,050 tokens (HTTP 400), so no score/rubric batches or large state.
ollama:tev1:4b.speed: ~1.5s mean/case (0.9-1.8s on 1-4 question cases), M2 Max warm, 2026-10-06
ollama:tev1:4b.tested: 2026-10-06 jev:compare vs human labels, on the 28 questions it accepted: 89% (choice 8/8, noul 85%), conf>=0.66 96%; Jev 27/28, qwen3.5:9b 27/28, nimble 26/28 on the same set. Skipped 3 of 17 cases (prompt >2050 tok: both templates cases, import-columns). Model license not stated on library page (scripts MIT); AI-LAB only. | 2026-10-06 cold start: first request 4.3s / 2.2s (spotlight-0), 3.9s / 1.9s (triage-0); warm 0.08-0.24s.

parakeet-pro:nvidia_parakeet-v3.when: Parakeet v3: throughput-oriented CoreML option for long recordings, 1.2 GB, drive-bound. Covers a European language set, not all of Whisper's; check before offering it for non-English.

qwen3-asr:qwen3-asr-1.7b.when: Qwen3-ASR 1.7B (Pro): accuracy-oriented, 30 languages plus 22 Chinese dialects, supports speaker recognition; the pick for Chinese. Drive-bound: 1.77 GB per the app, 1384 MB on disk. WHISPER_MODEL_EXTERNAL: selected for file, dictation and live on a flip to AI-LAB.
qwen3-asr:qwen3-asr-1.7b.tested: Vendor-positioned as accuracy-oriented and slower; not yet measured here.

whisper-cpp:ggml-model-whisper-base.en.when: English-only whisper-cpp (GGML, CPU), offline-safe. Non-English audio fails silently as fluent, wrong English.

whisper-cpp:ggml-model-whisper-small.en.when: English-only whisper-cpp (GGML, CPU), offline-safe. Non-English audio fails silently as fluent, wrong English.

whisper-cpp:ggml-model-whisper-tiny.en.when: English-only whisper-cpp (GGML, CPU), offline-safe. Non-English audio fails silently as fluent, wrong English.

whisperkit:openai_whisper-large-v3-v2024.when: Large v3 Turbo: accuracy-oriented multilingual WhisperKit, 1.5 GB, drive-bound (gone when AI-LAB is ejected).
whisperkit:openai_whisper-large-v3-v2024.tested: Not measured against Qwen3-ASR here; compare on the actual audio when accuracy decides it.

whisperkit:openai_whisper-small.when: Offline-safe multilingual default: the only multilingual model that survives an AI-LAB eject. 464 MB. WHISPER_MODEL_LOCAL, selected on a flip to local.
whisperkit:openai_whisper-small.tested: 2026-08-24: with the local store active, mw models list showed only small plus the .en set, and diarization still detected 2 speakers on a 120 s clip (before the second diarization bundle existed). No throughput measured yet.

ollama:gemma4:12b-nvfp4.when: Dense 12B, MLX. Pulled to test the Gemma 4 12B email pitch — did not beat gemma4:26b-nvfp4.
ollama:gemma4:12b-nvfp4.speed: 18 tok/s warm decode, 337 tok/s prompt eval
ollama:gemma4:12b-nvfp4.tested: Dense 12B slower per token than 26B MoE (4B active). Aider bug-fix 123s 4/4; pi bug-fix 176s 0/4 — pi diagnosed the bugs then never called the edit tool, leaked <|channel>thought artifacts.

ollama:gemma4:31b.tested: Thinking-model + dense architecture double-whammy. Burns ~150 tokens on internal reasoning every turn, then generates the answer at 6.5 tok/s. Unusable for interactive work. Reclaimed 19 GB. gemma4:26b-nvfp4 MoE covers the gemma role better in every way.

ollama:gemma4:latest.tested: Superseded by gemma4:26b-nvfp4 (MLX): 558 tok/s prompt eval (5x this) at similar decode speed. Same underlying 26B-a4b-it model; MLX quant is strictly faster on M2.

ollama:jt-voice-gemma-test:latest.tested: Test alias of gemma4:26b-nvfp4 (num_ctx 49152, temperature 0) for JT voice tests; weights fully shared with the base. Removed 2026-09-30, tests done.

ollama:jt-voice-muse-test:latest.tested: Test alias of muse-glimmer:latest (num_ctx 49152) for JT voice tests; weights fully shared with the base. Removed 2026-09-30, tests done.

ollama:nemotron-3.5-lightning:30b-mlx.when: Removed — too big for always-on setup; re-pull + bench if re-added (tail lost to a CLI truncation bug)
ollama:nemotron-3.5-lightning:30b-mlx.speed: never cleanly benched — OOM'd before measurement; MLX nvfp4 prefill path unknown
ollama:nemotron-3.5-lightning:30b-mlx.tested: 2026-08-12: 32.9B nvfp4/MLX (nemotron_h hybrid), thinking+tools, 262K ctx (tail lost to a CLI truncation bug)

ollama:nimble:9b-mlx-bf16.when: MLX bf16 build of nimble (17 GB on disk, needs Ollama >= 0.40). ~20% faster than nimble:9b-q4_K_M but 3x the disk and no accuracy gain. Prefer the q4_K_M GGUF.
ollama:nimble:9b-mlx-bf16.speed: ~4.2s mean/case vs 5.2s for q4_K_M (M2 Max warm, 17 fixtures, 2026-10-06); 13.7s cold warm-up
ollama:nimble:9b-mlx-bf16.tested: 2026-10-06 jev:compare vs human labels, 65 q: 72% (score 60%, choice 73%, noul 90%) vs q4_K_M 74% (63/73/90); same pick as q4_K_M on 63/65. Confident-subset accuracy 85% (n=47) vs 78% (n=59). AI-LAB only. | 2026-10-06 cold start (spotlight-0): first request 14.0s / 12.8s (load ~12.7-14.0s), warm ~0.02s. Slowest cold start of any Jev backend; 24 GB resident. | MLX build: ~same warm speed/accuracy as GGUF on Lindris jev:compare (2026-10-06), cold start 6–14s, 3x disk — removed.

ollama:nimble:9b-q4_K_M.when: Decision model for typed choice/yes-no/score via /v1/systemone only (not chat). Returns per-option probabilities, its one edge over qwen3.5:9b. Prompt (state+questions) HARD-capped at 8,192 tokens despite the 256K tag.
ollama:nimble:9b-q4_K_M.speed: ~2.0s per 1-question call at ~500 tok prompt, ~250 tok/s prefill, M2 Max warm (not the vendor's 100ms M5 Max figure); each extra question re-reads the prompt
ollama:nimble:9b-q4_K_M.tested: 2026-09-30: tied with qwen3.5:9b on session-state (91 ex): holdout 87% vs qwen 92%; at p(done)>=0.85 wrongly flagged 3/91 vs qwen 4/91, done found 60/68 vs 61/68. qwen via chat logprobs is faster (1.2-1.5s vs 2.0-2.3s) and already on both stores. No reason to keep 5.6GB. Bench: private/decision-model-bench/

ollama:qwen2.5-coder:1.5b-base.when: Base model (not chat-tuned). Pulled by mistake for cron use.
ollama:qwen2.5-coder:1.5b-base.tested: Base model has no instruction/chat tuning — can't follow prompts or tool-call formats. qwen2.5-coder:1.5b (chat-tuned) is the right variant for cron title generation.

ollama:qwen2.5-coder:7b-base.tested: Base model — no chat tuning. qwen2.5-coder:7b is the usable version.

ollama:qwen3.5:0.8b-nvfp4.when: Small MLX candidate to replace qwen2.5-coder:1.5b for cron title generation.
ollama:qwen3.5:0.8b-nvfp4.tested: Confirms MLX-prompt-eval-bottleneck on M2 is architecture-family-wide, not just the 35B: 100 tok/s prompt eval vs qwen2.5-coder:1.5b GGUF's 807. Decode is faster (182 vs 156) but for cron-style small-prompt tasks the prompt-eval loss dominates. Reclaimed 1 GB.

ollama:qwen3.5:35b-a3b-coding-nvfp4.when: Ollama's MLX-flagship coding model. Advertised 2x speedup vs GGUF.
ollama:qwen3.5:35b-a3b-coding-nvfp4.tested: qwen3.5+NVFP4+MLX combo hits a broken slow path on M2 — prompt eval 3 tok/s vs qwen3-coder GGUF's 110. Thinking-model verbosity compounds it (362-832 tokens per response). Blog's 2x speedup is M5-only (GPU Neural Accelerators). Reclaimed 22 GB.

ollama:tev1:4b-mlx-bf16.when: MLX bf16 build of tev1:4b (8.4 GB, needs Ollama >= 0.40). No gain over tev1:4b GGUF: same speed, no 2,050-token prompt cap but rejects choice questions with more than 24 candidates (Spotlight page picker). Prefer tev1:4b GGUF.
ollama:tev1:4b-mlx-bf16.speed: ~0.8s mean on the 6 cases both builds run (GGUF 0.80s), 0.6-5.2s overall; M2 Max warm, Ollama 0.40.0, 2026-10-06
ollama:tev1:4b-mlx-bf16.tested: 2026-10-06 jev:compare vs human labels: 72% on 57 accepted questions (noul 95%, choice 4/7, score 60%); 8 spotlight cases HTTP 400 'Tev1 supports at most 24 candidates'. Score questions run (GGUF skips them) but are poor (60%, Jev 53%). On the 20 shared questions: 17 same pick, GGUF 18 correct vs MLX 19. AI-LAB only. | 2026-10-06 cold start (triage-0; spotlight-0 rejected, >24 candidates): first request 7.5s / 6.2s, warm ~0.01s. Cold start 2-3x the GGUF build. | MLX build: ~same warm speed/accuracy as GGUF on Lindris jev:compare (2026-10-06), cold start 6–14s, 3x disk — removed.
